findings.evidence: specs/edexcel/physics-1PH0.md Appendix 2; grep for 'Fv' and 'force x speed' returns nothing

findings.claim: The three wires have standardised colours introduced with post-2006 wiring regulations
findings.truth: Brown / blue / green-and-yellow flex colours were harmonised in the UK in 1970. The 2004-06 change (BS 7671) recoloured fixed wiring, not appliance flex or plugs. Date claim removed.
findings.evidence: settled fact; spec 10.37-10.40 states the wires without any date

findings.claim: Question 6 typed '9 marks - Extended Response'.
findings.truth: Edexcel 1PH0 Paper 2 is ten questions worth 100 marks with extended open-response items at 6 marks. A 9-mark tariff is an AQA/Eduqas format and does not exist on this paper. Retyped as 6 marks; the same fault appears in L5, L6, L7 and L8.

findings.claim: The field is stronger close to the plates and weaker at the edges (edge effects).
findings.truth: Between parallel plates the field is uniform - equal strength everywhere - which is why the lines are drawn parallel and evenly spaced, as the same paragraph says. Only the fringe near the plate edges is weaker. The sentence contradicted itself and taught a misconception.

findings.claim: The unit's eight lessons cover topics 8, 9 (part), 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14. Topic 15 - Forces and matter - is absent.

summary: The known build fault is here in force: five of the seven higher-only wrappers are wrong. L2 hides moments, levers and gears (9.6P-9.9P), L5 hides the whole of static electricity (Topic 11), L8 hides absolute zero, the kelvin scale and Boyle's law (14.14-14.19P), and L7's wrapper swallows the both-tier National Grid and transformer power equation (13.8-13.10); only L6's d.c.-motor wrapper is right, and it was too narrow. Two wrappers are also added or widened where bold content sat open to Foundation: the free-body diagram section in L2 (9.3-9.5) and the motor-effect half of L6 (12.10-12.13). L5 also carries tier='higher' on the lesson row, so Foundation students cannot reach Topic 11 at all. Beyond tier: five questions carry a 9-mark tariff Edexcel never sets, two off-spec equations (P = Fv, P = V2/R) are taught as required recall, an exam claim rests on centre of mass which is not in 1PH0, a parallel-plate field is described as stronger near the plates, the plug-colour date is wrong, and three flashcards are broken. All arithmetic and every answer key recompute correctly. The one structural gap is Topic 15 (Forces and matter), which is taught nowhere in the subject, taking core practical 15.6 with it.
